subject: Post-call recap: HealthLytics retention carve‑out & residency ask
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Sousa <ana.sousa@healthlytics.eu>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 09:08:00 +0100
Subject: Post-call recap: HealthLytics retention carve‑out & residency ask

Hi Ana — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Summary of ask:
- HealthLytics needs strict PII handling for patient identifiers and wants an option to avoid persistent storage of request/response payloads (asking if 0‑retention is possible).
- EU data residency for all payloads and audit logs (primary: eu-west region).
- Shortened operational logs for debugging (30 days preferred, ideally less for PII-containing logs).

What we committed to investigate:
- Whether Redwood can support an exception to retain 0 copies of request/response payloads (ephemeral mode) while still providing enough telemetry for debugging and billing.
- Options across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private: exact tradeoffs for 0‑retention and residency.
- What documentation/evidence you need for procurement (DPA, SOC2 artifacts, logging matrix).

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share a small matrix outlining retention options and the technical caveats (attached: data_retention_matrix.xlsx).
2) Please confirm the absolute minimum telemetry you need (billing-only tokens vs. request metadata).
3) If you want to move forward, we’ll loop Legal/InfoSec and propose a draft DPA + SOW for the carveout.

Estimated timeline: we can get a formal DPA/SOW draft to you in 3 business days once we agree on the exact retention scope.

Are you available Wed (18th) for a 30-min follow-up to review the matrix?

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: data_retention_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Ana Sousa <ana.sousa@healthlytics.eu>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marie Dupont <marie.dupont@healthlytics.eu>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 11:35:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: HealthLytics retention carve‑out & residency ask

Thanks Rishi — useful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Zero retention requirement: for any payload containing direct patient identifiers (name, national id, MRN) we require no persistent storage beyond immediate inference execution. That effectively means we need either an on‑prem/private deployment or a contractual guarantee for hosted ephemeral processing.

2) Logs and debug traces: we can accept aggregated telemetry for performance/billing (e.g., token counts, latency) retained up to 30 days. However, stack traces or debug dumps that could include sample payloads must be restricted to 7 days and only accessible to a named set of engineers with MFA.

3) Data residency: all processing and storage must occur in EU regions. We cannot accept US‑hosted processing for PII.

Procurement asks: please send any templates you have for DPA and a redlineable SOW that includes the retention carveout and IL4‑style personnel controls. I’ve attached our security checklist for reference.

We’d like a legal point of contact from Redwood to start the DPA discussion.

Best,
Ana Sousa
Head of Platform Security | HealthLytics
ana.sousa@healthlytics.eu | +44 20 7946 0123

Attachment: healthlytics_security_requirements.pdf (security checklist)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Sousa <ana.sousa@healthlytics.eu>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marie Dupont <marie.dupont@healthlytics.eu>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 08:20:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: HealthLytics retention carve‑out & residency ask

Hi Ana — appreciate the clarity. Looping in Aditya (SE) and Lauren (my manager) so we can give a concrete proposal. High-level options we see that map to your asks: 

Option A — Private deployment (recommended for strict PII control):
- Private control plane inside your VPC or our EU private cluster.
- Ephemeral processing option: request/response payloads never written to disk; only in-memory during inference.
- Audit logs stored in region (eu‑west) in a customer‑managed S3 for full control.
- Will require a deployment window and ops coordination.

Option B — Dedicated capacity (Redwood-managed but isolated):
- Dedicated GPU pool in EU region.
- Can contractually require ephemeral mode for request/response (we’d put controls in the DPA + SOW).
- Some operational telemetry (metrics, token counts) retained for billing; we can scope debug artifacts to 7 days and narrow access.

Option C — Hosted API with contractual carveout (fastest to ship, riskier for strict PII):
- We can offer an ephemeral processing exception for hosted with a signed DPA, but this requires stronger legal limits and attestation (SOC2 + supplemental controls) and may not be feasible for all workload types.

Immediate ask from Redwood: can you confirm whether you need the solution live by end of March? That will determine whether we push for Dedicated vs Private and what procurement timeline is realistic.

Proposed MAP (mutual action plan):
- Thu 19 Feb: Redwood to share technical logging options & DPA draft (we’ll attach the redwood_dpa_draft.pdf).
- Mon 23 Feb: HealthLytics to confirm selected option and minimal telemetry list.
- Wed 25 Feb: Legal to exchange redlines and target final SOW sign by Mar 5.

We’ll also include a short addendum that specifies which internal Redwood roles can access debug artifacts and how access is audited.

Happy to hop on the 18th or 19th for 30 minutes — please propose a time.

Thanks,
Rishi

---
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ana Sousa <ana.sousa@healthlytics.eu>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marie Dupont <marie.dupont@healthlytics.eu>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:12:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: HealthLytics retention carve‑out & residency ask

Hi Ana / team — Aditya here (SE). Adding a few technical details so you can evaluate feasibility: 

Types of logs and how we can control them:
- Request/response payloads: can be kept in RAM only and never flushed to disk on Private deployments. For Dedicated/Hosted we support an "ephemeral mode" where payloads are not written to persistent storage; this mode requires contractual DPA guarantees and will disable certain async tooling (e.g., long‑term extractors for fine‑tuning).
- KV cache / prompt caching: can be configured to persist or be ephemeral per model instance; if you need zero persistence we can disable caching (with CPU/latency cost).
- Operational audit logs (auth events, job lifecycle): default retention = 30 days. We can reduce to 7 days for logs that may include PII if you sign the DPA and accept reduced debug windows.
- Access controls: named role access, enforced MFA, and IRM for debug bundle downloads. We log all downloads and retain those audit records for 365 days.

Technical caveats:
- 0‑retention for payloads eliminates the ability to replay problematic requests for root cause analysis. We recommend a small workstream to define emergency debug procedures (time‑boxed capture with explicit approval).
- Some third‑party integrations (monitoring agents) may impose additional minimal storage — we can whitelist/inventory them for you.

Attached is a short capabilities document and an example config snippet for ephemeral mode (redwood_logging_options.pdf). Happy to run a 30‑minute technical session to walk through options and impacts on latency/cost.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_logging_options.pdf
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:42:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: HealthLytics retention carve‑out & residency ask

Hi Ana — looping in formally from the Redwood leadership side. Thank you for outlining the requirements so clearly. We are prepared to proceed with a carveout under the following commercial and compliance conditions: 

1) Execution of Redwood DPA with the 0‑retention addendum (attached: redwood_dpa_draft.pdf).
2) Agreement to a scoped SOW (attached: SOW-HL-042.docx) that defines which endpoints will run in ephemeral mode, the emergency debug approval flow, and the named list of engineers with debug access.

Compliance asks we will meet before production cutover:
- Provide SOC2 Type II report and supplementary control narrative for ephemeral processing (we will share SOC2 artifacts with your Security team under NDA).
- Perform a short security walkthrough with your platform security team prior to sign-off.

Commercial note: given the additional operational constraints, we can provide a one-time implementation credit (to offset deployment effort) and standard enterprise pricing for Dedicated or Private. 

Next steps I propose: 
- Rishi to send DPA + SOW (done).
- Marie / Ana to propose legal redlines within 5 business days.
- Aditya to schedule a technical walkthrough (30–45 min) next week.

If those timelines are acceptable we’ll prepare an internal change request to prioritize the HL-042 deployment. 

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_dpa_draft.pdf, SOW-HL-042.docx
